Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test "testUnionOfVariableAndNode" sets up an XPath context with a variable "var" holding a string value "varValue", and then tries to iterate pointers using the XPath expression "$var | /MAIN/A". This expression attempts to union a variable reference with a node-set selected from the XML document.

The current bug report states that there is a JXPathException: "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree: '$var' and ''". This happens in NodePointer.compareNodePointers, indicating that when comparing pointers to order nodes as part of union operations, pointers belonging to different trees are being compared.

The method NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer p1, int depth1, NodePointer p2, int depth2) recursively compares two node pointers by moving up their parent chain to the root. If it reaches the top level (depth1 == 1) without finding a common root, it throws the exception about pointers not belonging to the same tree.

The test case's XPath "$var | /MAIN/A" mixes a variable pointer (to the String "varValue") and pointers to nodes in the XML tree (under MAIN/A). The variable pointer's root is different from the XML nodes' root, so comparing them causes this exception.

Hence, the bug is caused by the union operation ($var | /MAIN/A) trying to merge pointers from different underlying models/trees (the variable "var" and XML nodes), which leads to the comparator in NodePointer failing with an exception because it cannot compare nodes across different trees.

Recent bug reports are not directly relevant since they focus on namespaces and value trimming, not on pointer comparisons or unions.

In brief: The XPath union operator tries to compare node pointers from variable-contained values and XML nodes. Since these pointers belong to different trees, an exception is thrown due to the lack of a mechanism to compare or unify pointers across different tree contexts.

This suggests the code handling union operations and pointer comparisons in JXPath lacks support to handle mixing variables and node sets in expressions like "$var | /MAIN/A" without throwing exceptions. A fix would involve modifying how such unions are handled to avoid invalid cross-tree pointer comparisons.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
